method: Hand-written single-best-answer MCQs grounded only in the accepted open full text.

topic.topicDisplayName: SLE: SLICC 2012 and ACR/EULAR 2019 classification criteria compared
topic.coverageNote: Direct comparison of the 2019 structure with SLICC 2012 and ACR 1997. The SLICC derivation paper alone cannot describe the 2019 criteria.

mcqs.question: What immunologic rule did SLICC 2012 add, as summarized in the 2019 paper?

options.A: At least one immunologic criterion is required, and histology-compatible nephritis plus ANA or anti-dsDNA is sufficient to classify SLE
options.C: Four clinical criteria and no antibodies
options.D: Anti-Sm is mandatory in every case

mcqs.correctAnswerText: At least one immunologic criterion is required, and histology-compatible nephritis plus ANA or anti-dsDNA is sufficient to classify SLE
mcqs.explanation: SLICC required at least one immunologic criterion and allowed histology-proven compatible nephritis plus ANA or anti-dsDNA to classify SLE.

sourceRefs.excerpt: requiring at least one immunological criterion to be present, and categorized histology-proven nephritis compatible with SLE as sufficient for classification, if anti-nuclear antibodies (ANA) or antibodies to double-stranded DNA (dsDNA) were present.

mcqs.question: How did SLICC sensitivity and specificity compare with the 1997 ACR criteria?

options.C: Both sensitivity and specificity were higher

mcqs.explanation: SLICC increased sensitivity and had lower specificity than the 1997 ACR criteria.

sourceRefs.excerpt: While achieving their goal of increasing sensitivity, the SLICC criteria have lower specificity than the 1997 ACR criteria

mcqs.question: Why did the 2019 criteria use a positive ANA as an entry criterion?

options.A: ANA has high sensitivity and limited specificity, and the structure was thought to reflect SLE pathogenesis
options.C: ANA-negative SLE is the most common subset

mcqs.correctAnswerText: ANA has high sensitivity and limited specificity, and the structure was thought to reflect SLE pathogenesis
mcqs.explanation: A positive ANA entry criterion was chosen to reflect pathogenesis and ANA's high sensitivity with limited specificity.

sourceRefs.excerpt: Such an approach was thought to reflect underlying SLE pathogenesis, and take into account ANA test characteristics of high sensitivity and limited specificity.

mcqs.question: Why were 2019 criteria weighted rather than counted equally?

options.A: Items are not equally useful; mucosal ulcers and biopsy-proven nephritis were the example given
options.B: Weights were required by regulators and have no clinical meaning
options.C: Every item has the same weight by design

mcqs.correctAnswerText: Items are not equally useful; mucosal ulcers and biopsy-proven nephritis were the example given
mcqs.explanation: Individual criteria were not expected to be equally useful, for example mucosal ulcers versus biopsy-proven lupus nephritis, so weighted criteria were developed.

sourceRefs.excerpt: we expected individual criteria would not be of equal utility (weight) for the classification of

mcqs.question: In whom do existing SLE classification criteria perform better, according to this paper?

options.A: Longstanding disease more than new-onset SLE
options.B: New-onset disease more than longstanding disease
options.E: Performance does not vary by disease duration

mcqs.correctAnswerText: Longstanding disease more than new-onset SLE
mcqs.explanation: Existing criteria perform better in longstanding disease than in new-onset SLE, which is why the 2019 project enriched samples for early disease.

sourceRefs.excerpt: Existing SLE classification criteria perform better in patients with longstanding disease than in new-onset SLE
